## HIGH-priority finding details

### H-1: `gap_analysis_model` front-matter key no longer parsed or consumed  (3/3 runs)
- **Docs**: Six pages described gap analysis defaulting to a cheaper `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` model, overridable via `gap_analysis_model:` in `WORKFLOW.md` front matter.
- **Source**: `ai-implement/src/workflow-md.ts:13` — accepted-keys list is `["model", "setup", "verify", "teardown"]`; `post-push-review.ts:746` resolves the gap-analysis model as the same value used for implementation, with no haiku fallback anywhere in source.
- **Edit**: Removed the dead-key accordion/examples and haiku-default claims across all six pages; rewrote model-selection sections to point at `models.implement`/`models.review` in `.ai-implement/config.yml`.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in all runs.

### H-2: `comment-trigger.yml` removed by sync; orchestrator webhook now handles `/ai-implement`  (3/3 runs)
- **Docs**: Nine pages described `comment-trigger.yml` as a file the workflow sync installs, and/or as the mechanism that always handles `/ai-implement` PR comments.
- **Source**: `ai-implement/src/workflow-sync.ts` — `REMOVE_FILES` unconditionally removes `comment-trigger.yml` on every sync; `src/webhook.ts`'s `handleIssueCommentWebhook` now dispatches `/ai-implement` directly via the orchestrator's own webhook on repos with current templates. Only legacy repos still carrying the old file use the old path.
- **Edit**: Updated all nine pages to frame `comment-trigger.yml` as legacy/removed-by-sync, name the webhook (`GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` + `issue_comment` subscription) as the current mechanism, and correct troubleshooting/setup guidance that told readers to sync to install the file.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in all runs.

### H-3: `dependency-auth` built-in pipeline step entirely undocumented  (3/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `customize/custom-steps.mdx`'s built-in step list and pipeline-order tip omitted this step.
- **Source**: A real pipeline step between `install-skills` and `install`, active only when a project has Dependency Token Scope enabled; fetches a short-lived cross-repo credential and installs it as a git credential helper.
- **Edit**: Added a `dependency-auth` accordion (with a working cross-link to the mapping field that gates it) and included it in the "not types of their own" note and pipeline-wiring tip.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in all runs.

### H-4: Dispatch circuit breaker (`DISPATCH_BREAKER_THRESHOLD`, "parked issues") entirely undocumented  (3/3 runs)
- **Docs**: Not mentioned on `configuration/environment-variables.mdx` or `reference/admin-ui.mdx`.
- **Source**: `ai-implement/src/dispatch-breaker.ts:4` parks an issue after N consecutive failed dispatches (default 3; 0 disables); surfaced in the admin UI's Runners panel with an unpark action.
- **Edit**: Added a `DISPATCH_BREAKER_THRESHOLD` `<ParamField>` and a "Parked issues" paragraph on the Runners section, cross-linked to each other.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in all runs.

### H-5: Admin UI Reports, Deployments, and Access panels entirely undocumented  (3/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `reference/admin-ui.mdx`'s sidebar summary and section list omitted all three, not even counted among the acknowledged placeholder pages.
- **Source**: `ai-implement/src/admin-ui/sidebar.ts` lists all three as real, non-stub routes backed by their own page modules and `admin.ts` endpoints.
- **Edit**: Added `### Reports`, `### Deployments`, and `### Access` sections with their KPI cards, actions, and API endpoints; updated the sidebar-group listing.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in all runs.

### H-6: Skill roster undercounted — 5 of 13 shipped skills missing  (3/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `skills/introduction.mdx`'s roster table and `skills/installation.mdx`'s "all eight" language covered only 8 skills.
- **Source**: `skills-source/plugin/skills/` has 13 directories with a real `SKILL.md` (`bd-shared` confirmed internal-only); `bd-high-plan`, `bd-kg-create`, `bd-kg-refresh`, `bd-kg-search`, and `bd-system-questions` were entirely missing.
- **Edit**: Added all five to the roster table and count on both pages; corrected the "six of the eight" feature-branch-grouping stat to "six of the thirteen" (verified unchanged by the new additions).
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in all runs.

### H-7: Dedup window documented as a fixed 24-hour TTL  (2/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `reference/admin-ui.mdx`, `how-it-works.mdx`, and `reference/error-codes.mdx` all described a 24-hour re-dispatch window.
- **Source**: `ai-implement/src/dedup.ts:119-124` — the `dispatched` table is a bare existence check with no expiry column; an entry clears only via a failed/timed-out run, the reconcile loop reaching a terminal issue, or a manual delete.
- **Edit**: Rewrote all three pages' dedup descriptions around the real clearing conditions, with no time-based expiry language.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in the 2 runs that flagged it; run-3 did not surface this finding.

### H-8: Self-deploy feature entirely undocumented  (2/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `FLY_DEPLOY_TOKEN`, the `AI_IMPLEMENT_SOURCE_*` build stamps, and the "Deployment available" notification never appeared on any page.
- **Source**: `ai-implement/.env.example`; `src/notify.ts:48-56,96-102` (`DeployNotification` "available" kind).
- **Edit**: Added a Self-deploy accordion to `configuration/environment-variables.mdx`, a Self-deploy section to `setup/deploy.mdx`, and a note to `reference/notifications.mdx`.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in the 2 runs that flagged it; run-2 did not surface this finding (it rated the underlying env vars MEDIUM only where flagged at all).

### H-9: MCP/KG orchestrator env vars undocumented  (3/3 runs, priority disputed)
- **Docs**: `configuration/environment-variables.mdx` had no entries for `KG_SIDECAR_URL`, `KG_SOURCE_REPO`, `MEMORY_PROVIDER`, `MCP_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_ORIGINS`, or `MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL`.
- **Source**: `ai-implement/.env.example:154-182`; `src/mcp-oauth.ts:30,155`. These back a real, optional advanced feature (the `/mcp` endpoint and its knowledge-graph sidecar).
- **Edit**: Added an "MCP server and knowledge graph (advanced)" accordion covering all five variables.
- **Priority agreement**: Rated MEDIUM independently by run-1 (split across two items) and run-2, but bundled into a HIGH finding by run-3 (grouped with the dispatch breaker and self-deploy, both undisputed HIGH). Kept HIGH per the no-downgrade rule. See Synthesis decisions log for the reasoning.

### H-10: `dependencyTokenScope` mapping field missing from field reference  (2/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `configuration/team-repo-mappings.mdx` describes itself as the full field reference but omitted this field.
- **Source**: `ai-implement/src/config.ts:72-73` — a real, UI-exposed, security-relevant setting (installation-wide read access to private sibling repos, all-or-nothing).
- **Edit**: Added a `<ParamField>` with a `<Warning>` describing the all-or-nothing scope and the publicly-reachable-orchestrator requirement.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in the 2 runs that flagged it; run-3 did not surface this finding.

### H-11: Jira blocking-semantics claim was backwards  (2/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `reference/labels.mdx` stated Jira has no built-in blocking semantics.
- **Source**: `ai-implement/src/providers/jira.ts:143-151,259-262` (`isBlockedByIncomplete`) — an open "Blocks" link is enforced during polling, mirroring Linear's blocking check; the match is on Jira's default link-type name and fails open if renamed.
- **Edit**: Replaced the false claim with an accurate description, including the rename/fail-open caveat.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in the 2 runs that flagged it; run-3 did not surface this finding.

### H-12: Tracker-support table wrongly categorizes which skills get dedicated Jira handling  (2/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `skills/introduction.mdx` credited some skills with "dedicated Jira handling" while describing `bd-build-up`'s support as merely "projected" from Linear.
- **Source**: `skills-source/plugin/skills/bd-shared/README.md` and per-skill `SKILL.md` files show `bd-build-up` and `bd-mega-build-up` share dedicated tracker adapters (not projected); `bd-super-build-down` inherits `bd-build-down`'s dedicated handling. Only `bd-summit-push` is genuinely projected.
- **Edit**: Regrouped the tracker-support paragraph to reflect the real categorization, independently re-verified against source.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in the 2 runs that flagged it, though they described the miscategorization slightly differently (run-1: `bd-build-up`/`bd-super-build-down` wrongly excluded; run-2: `bd-build-up` wrongly split from `bd-mega-build-up`). Run-3 did not surface this finding.

### H-13: Post-push review comment format/mechanics were stale  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: Five pages described a single static PR comment with "Implemented / Gaps / Manual Steps Required" sections.
- **Source**: `ai-implement/src/pipeline/steps/post-push-review.ts:741-1141` — the real step is an iterative review→fix loop (up to 3 passes by default) posting "✅ Approved" or "⚠️ Reviewer found issues — starting fix pass," force-pushing revisions as needed.
- **Edit**: Rewrote `reference/gap-analysis.mdx` (retitled around the actual loop) and updated the corresponding mentions on `how-it-works.mdx`, `introduction.mdx`, `quickstart.mdx`, and the `post-push-review` accordion in `customize/custom-steps.mdx`.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH; only run-1 surfaced this finding.

### H-14: Planning comment schema stale  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: Described four comments (Architecture Analysis, Test Plan, Work Units, Cross-Story Context) and a parallel-subagent implementation trigger.
- **Source**: `ai-implement/workflows/PLANNING.md:50-56,117-172` — the current template and parser produce exactly three comments (Implementation Map, Acceptance Bar, Risks & Open Questions); no subagent fan-out exists in the pipeline.
- **Edit**: Rewrote the comment-type sections in `customize/planning-md.mdx`, `configuration/planning.mdx`, and `how-it-works.mdx`, including frontmatter descriptions that still referenced the old schema.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH; only run-1 surfaced this finding.

### H-15: False prerequisite — "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests"  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `setup/github-app.mdx` and `quickstart.mdx` told readers this repo setting was required or PR creation would fail.
- **Source**: Every synced workflow authenticates as the installed GitHub App and uses its own token for PR operations — a separate identity from the `github-actions[bot]` actor that toggle governs.
- **Edit**: Removed the false prerequisite section from `setup/github-app.mdx`; replaced the warning in `quickstart.mdx` with an accurate note.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH; only run-1 surfaced this finding.

### H-16: Runner image "publicly pullable" claim wrong for GitHub Actions mode  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `customize/runner-image.mdx` stated images must be publicly pullable, unconditionally.
- **Source**: True only for Fly Machines/local Docker. GitHub Actions mode pulls using the job's own token and separately validates the resolved image against a trusted-prefix allowlist, hard-failing outside it.
- **Edit**: Scoped the "publicly pullable" claim to Fly Machines/local Docker and documented the GitHub Actions allowlist and its override variable.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH; only run-1 surfaced this finding.

### H-17: `WORKFLOW.md` starter template contradicted the git-ownership model  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: The example template shown told Claude to create a branch, commit, and open a PR.
- **Source**: `ai-implement/workflows/WORKFLOW.md:128-166` — the real template instructs Claude to leave changes uncommitted; the pipeline owns every commit, push, and PR.
- **Edit**: Replaced the starter-template listing with the actual current file.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH; only run-1 surfaced this finding.

### H-18: SSO docs omit the role model and MCP's role-blind access  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `setup/sso.mdx` covered only provider auth and allowlist matching.
- **Source**: Every admitted identity carries a role (`admin`/`user`); `user` needs explicit page grants for the admin UI, but MCP access at `/mcp` is role-blind.
- **Edit**: Added a "Roles and page access" section, independently verified against `access-entries.ts` and `mcp.ts`.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH; only run-1 surfaced this finding.

### H-19: Domain-vs-address role distinction omitted (lockout risk)  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `OAUTH_ALLOWED_DOMAINS` and `OAUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS` were presented as interchangeable.
- **Source**: `ai-implement/src/access-entries.ts:169-176` — a domain entry always seeds as `user`; only an individual address can seed as `admin`.
- **Edit**: Added a warning to the new "Roles and page access" section.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH; only run-1 surfaced this finding.

### H-20: `${PLANNING_CONTEXT}` double-emission risk undocumented  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `customize/workflow-md.mdx`'s variable table listed the token with no caveat.
- **Source**: The shipped template's own comment (`WORKFLOW.md:39-41`) warns that the implementation step appends this block automatically, so referencing the token in the body duplicates it.
- **Edit**: Added a Warning to the variables table.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH; only run-1 surfaced this finding.

### H-21: Notification completion-status enumeration omitted `review_failed`  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `reference/notifications.mdx` listed only `completed`, `failed`, `timed_out`.
- **Source**: `ai-implement/src/notify.ts:31-46` — `CompletionNotification.status` is a four-value union including `review_failed`, with its own label and icon.
- **Edit**: Updated the completion-notification description to list all four outcomes.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH; only run-1 surfaced this finding.

### H-22: Repo-variable run caps documented as generally effective; legacy-only in reality  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `configuration/environment-variables.mdx` and `configuration/team-repo-mappings.mdx` presented `AI_IMPLEMENT_MAX_TURNS`/`_MAX_ITERATIONS`/`_MAX_JOB_MINUTES` as capping all `/ai-implement` comment-triggered runs.
- **Source**: `ai-implement/src/comment-gapfill-drain.ts:184-185` — the webhook-driven dispatch path reads the mapping's own `maxTurns`/`maxIterations` directly, never these repo variables, which are legacy-only.
- **Edit**: Added notes to both pages clarifying these variables only take effect on a repo still carrying the legacy `comment-trigger.yml` workflow.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH; only run-2 surfaced this finding.

### H-23: `verify` hook wrongly described as gating PR creation  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `customize/workflow-md.mdx` described `verify:` as validation that must pass before the PR is opened.
- **Source**: Pipeline order has `push` before `verify`; the PR is already open by the time `verify` runs — a failure fails the job but doesn't prevent or close the PR.
- **Edit**: Corrected the claim to match reality and `custom-steps.mdx`'s own already-accurate description.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH; only run-2 surfaced this finding.

### H-24: Admin API reference wrongly claims universal bearer-token requirement  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `reference/admin-ui.mdx` stated all `/api/*` endpoints except `/api/auth` require a bearer token.
- **Source**: `ai-implement/src/index.ts:2890-2975` — several runner-callback and webhook endpoints explicitly bypass bearer auth, using their own per-run tokens or HMAC signatures instead.
- **Edit**: Corrected the claim and cross-referenced the alternate-auth endpoint sections.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH; only run-2 surfaced this finding.

### H-25: Docs wrongly claim the New Project stepper's Capacity step exposes run-cap fields  (1/3 runs)

## Synthesis decisions log (audit-trail for reviewers)

### H-1
- **Present in:** Run 1 HIGH, Run 2 HIGH, Run 3 HIGH
- **Dedup reasoning:** All three cite the same accepted-keys list in `workflow-md.ts` and the same absence of a haiku fallback in `post-push-review.ts`; titles and exact page sets differed but the underlying drift is identical.
- **Selected edit from:** Run 2 for the provider pages (most complete: explicit "key does not exist" note plus a working link to the real mechanism); Run 1 as the base for `workflow-md.mdx` merged with Run 2's fixes (subagent-verified); Run 1 as the base for `gap-analysis.mdx` since it's bundled into that page's larger H-13 rewrite.
- **Selection reasoning:** Run 3's fix was accurate but the least detailed of the three (no pointer to the real per-phase mechanism), so it lost on the provider pages; its content was otherwise consistent with the other two, so no facts were lost by not selecting it.

**Edit candidates compared:**

Run 2's approach on `providers/anthropic.mdx` (selected):
```mdx
- The gap analysis step runs on that same model. There is no separate, cheaper
  default for it, and `gap_analysis_model:` is not a recognized front-matter key.
```

Run 3's approach (not selected):
```mdx
- The gap analysis step runs on the same model as implementation — the model:
  value above, or claude-sonnet-4-6 when that is unset. There is no separate
  cheaper default for gap analysis.
```

### H-2
- **Present in:** Run 1 HIGH (H-17), Run 2 HIGH (H-1, H-2, H-3), Run 3 HIGH (H-5)
- **Dedup reasoning:** Run 2 split this into three findings (sync file-list change, webhook-required, gap-fill-trigger docs) that all trace to the same two source facts (`workflow-sync.ts`'s `REMOVE_FILES`, `webhook.ts`'s `handleIssueCommentWebhook`); Run 1 and Run 3 each treated it as one finding. Merged into a single canonical finding per the "same underlying drift, different docs surfaces" rule — this is the largest cluster in the audit, touching nine files.
- **Selected edit from:** Per-file, chosen independently by subagents given the same source-fact briefing: labels.mdx (Run 2 + Run 3 merged), github-app.mdx (Run 1 + Run 3 merged), quickstart.mdx (Run 1 + Run 2 merged), target-repo.mdx (Run 2), troubleshooting.mdx (Run 3's substance + Run 2's checklist), workflow-templates.mdx (Run 1 + Run 2 merged), environment-variables.mdx (Run 2, main-loop selection), how-it-works.mdx (Run 1 + Run 2 merged), gap-analysis.mdx (Run 1, verified complete).
- **Selection reasoning:** No single run's candidate was complete on every touched file; each subagent independently verified claims against `workflow-sync.ts`/`webhook.ts`/`CLAUDE.md` before merging, catching and rejecting one incorrect blanket claim (Run 2 on `setup/github-app.mdx` implied *all* repos now require the webhook, omitting the legitimate legacy-repo carve-out that Run 3 got right).

### H-3
- **Present in:** Run 1 HIGH, Run 2 HIGH, Run 3 HIGH
- **Dedup reasoning:** All three cite the same undocumented pipeline step at the same source location.
- **Selected edit from:** Run 1's accordion text (main-loop selection) — the only candidate that cross-links to `dependencyTokenScope` on `team-repo-mappings.mdx` using the correct `#param-` anchor prefix per this repo's anchor rules; Run 2's `reviewCheckNames` ParamField was added on top (see H-28) since Run 1 didn't cover that key.
- **Selection reasoning:** Run 2's prose had more implementation detail (`COMPOSER_AUTH`, git credential helper internals) but no cross-link; Run 1's cross-link was judged more valuable to a reader deciding whether to enable Dependency Token Scope than the extra technical detail, which is arguably too implementation-focused per this repo's "no internal vocabulary" rule.

**Edit candidates compared:**

Run 1's approach (selected):
```mdx
<Accordion title="dependency-auth">
  Mints a short-lived, read-only cross-repo GitHub token for projects with
  Dependency Token Scope enabled, so the install step can reach private
  sibling repos. Skipped automatically when the project doesn't have this
  enabled — see [`dependencyTokenScope`](/latest/configuration/team-repo-mappings#param-dependency-token-scope).
</Accordion>
```

Run 2's approach (not selected):
```mdx
<Accordion title="dependency-auth">
  Fetches a short-lived, read-only GitHub credential for private sibling
  repositories and installs it as a git credential helper (and
  COMPOSER_AUTH) before install runs. Automatically skipped unless the
  project mapping's Dependency Token Scope is set.
</Accordion>
```
